biological_question: Can combined sexual function maintain male mating success while physical sex separation shifts effective pollen delivery; does temporal mate opportunity predict realized paternity?

mating_display_2006.citation: Vamosi JC, Vamosi SM & Barrett SCH (2006). Sex in advertising: dioecy alters the net benefits of attractiveness in Sagittaria latifolia (Alismataceae). Proceedings of the Royal Society B 273:2401-2407.
mating_display_2006.experiment: Common garden pollinator-visit sequences in monoecious vs dioecious arrays, 20 trials × 4 individuals (80 plant appearances); male/female floral spatial arrangement differs
mating_display_2006.measurement_level: Foraging sequences and potential interplant pollen delivery, not actual deposited pollen, genetic paternity, seed fitness or rare-type invasion
mating_display_2006.dependence_warning: 4 plant appearances per array ×20 trials, 872 foraging trips nested by arrays/visitors; NOT 872 independent genotype invasions
mating_display_2006.causal_scope: Manipulated array sexual system and display across 20 experimental trials; effect on visit-sequence proxy, not naturally evolved sexual-system genotype treatment

natural_bateman_2022.citation: Kwok A & Dorken ME (2022). Sexual selection on male but not female function in monoecious and dioecious populations of broadleaf arrowhead (Sagittaria latifolia). Proceedings of the Royal Society B 289:20220919.
natural_bateman_2022.authors_interpretation: Synchronous protogyny makes monoecious inflorescences functionally unisexual at a particular time; male sexual selection can operate similarly under the two population sexual systems
claims_to_avoid: Similar observed gradients do not statistically certify equivalence across populations
Bateman β is association of mating with reproductive success conditional on clone size, not complete genotype lifetime fitness
Only four monoecious MLLs were recovered as both mothers and sires, preventing cross-sex-effect estimation
Raw versus size-adjusted regression estimates are different estimands; sign change should not be claimed as ecological causal effect

temporal_opportunity_2023.citation: Kwok A, Stephens S & Dorken ME (2023). Male reproductive success is not strongly affected by phenological changes in mate availability in monoecious Sagittaria latifolia. Royal Society Open Science 10:231117.
temporal_opportunity_2023.design: Natural monoecious flowering cohort; per-date male/female flower numbers used to construct pollen-transfer opportunity index, microsatellite paternity used for actual siring, dates nested by genet
temporal_opportunity_2023.theoretical_opportunity_time_variation: Significant seasonal changes in floral sex allocation and calculated pollen-transfer opportunity
temporal_opportunity_2023.empirical_result: Realized paternal success did not show detected association with timing or modelled pollen-transfer opportunity
temporal_opportunity_2023.alternative_explanation: Authors suggest nonrandom male sexual selection, local spatial pollen dispersal, and genotype size may account for missing opportunity-to-fitness relationship
temporal_opportunity_2023.dependence_warning: Repeated date × genets observations, 2013 population; not experimental genetic invasion, and n=52 assigned sires differs from n=39 analysis genets

selfing_inbreeding_2002.citation: Dorken ME, Friedman J & Barrett SCH (2002). The evolution and maintenance of monoecy and dioecy in Sagittaria latifolia (Alismataceae). Evolution 56:31-41.
selfing_inbreeding_2002.original_conclusion: Selfing substantially more common in monoecy; strong inbreeding depression in both, similar marker variation, differentiation and ecological sorting of systems
selfing_inbreeding_2002.caveat: Population-level marker-derived quantities, not individual lifetime pedigrees, independent causal selfing effect or same populations as 2006/2022/2023

structural_division_alternatives: Monoecious plant with temporally separated male and female flowers
Dioecious population with distinct male and female individuals
inference_contract.no_morph_equation: Monoecy is not a bisexual flower: the sexes are separated at the organ/flower level already
inference_contract.candidate_relative_pairing: One rare dioecious male plus one rare dioecious female are NOT the same single mutant genotype. Two loci and population genetic pairing must be modeled before comparing rare establishment.
inference_contract.study_dependence: Repeated Sagittaria genus and partially overlapping field research teams, differing cohorts and estimands, not four independent sex-system evolutionary origins
